headline: 13-year-old killed over his iPhone in Cumilla; 3 arrested
summary: Police arrested three suspects, including a 19-year-old and two teenagers, after Ishiat Shahriar Opratim was allegedly beaten to death during a phone snatching attempt.
details: Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class 7 student, was allegedly killed in the Sananda area of Cumilla after suspects attempted to snatch his iPhone.

Cumilla Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman stated that the suspects, including 19-year-old Saiful Islam Tuhin and two 15-year-olds, allegedly struck Opratim on the head with sticks during a scuffle.
Opratim had left home on Friday to take photos with friends when he went missing. His body was discovered by locals in the Sananda area of Lalmai Hill the following day.
Police used CCTV footage to identify Tuhin and later recovered the stolen iPhone from his home during a raid.
The victim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and KM Firoz Shahriar.
The Home Minister has assured that the government will assist in ensuring a speedy trial for the killing of the young boy.

headline_marked: ICT [[accepts charges against Zafar Iqbal, DU ex-VC Kamal]] and 6 others
headline: ICT accepts charges against Zafar Iqbal, DU ex-VC Kamal and 6 others
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has issued arrest warrants for eight people, including a noted writer and a former DU vice-chancellor, over crimes against humanity during the July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has taken cognisance of formal charges against eight individuals, including writer Dr Muhammad Zafar Iqbal and former Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor ASM Maksud Kamal, in a crimes against humanity case.
The charges relate to the killing of five people and injuries to approximately 300 others during the 2024 July Uprising in areas including Dhaka University, Nilkhet, and Azimpur.

The tribunal has issued arrest warrants for all eight accused. While three—retired judge AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik, Professor AKM Jamal Uddin, and Tanbir Hasan Shaikat—are already in custody, the others remain absconding.
Prosecution alleges that Maksud Kamal facilitated the involvement of Chhatra League activists in attacks on students after communicating with then-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Dr Zafar Iqbal is accused of referring to protesting students as 'Razakars' and remaining silent during the killings, with prosecutors claiming evidence of his involvement in a conspiracy.
Justice Manik is accused of justifying police shootings by calling a victim, Abu Sayed, a 'terrorist' on a talk show, which the prosecution says legitimised further suppression.
Professor Jamal Uddin allegedly called for students to be 'drowned' in the Bay of Bengal and 'eliminated'.
The other accused, including BCL leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, are alleged to have directly participated in attacks on protesters.
caption:
Arrest warrants issued for 8 people, including Zafar Iqbal and ex-DU VC Maksud Kamal, over July Uprising killings.

The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has taken cognisance of formal charges against eight individuals, including writer Dr Muhammad Zafar Iqbal and former Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor ASM Maksud Kamal, in a crimes against humanity case.

The charges relate to the killing of five people and injuries to approximately 300 others during the 2024 July Uprising in areas including Dhaka University, Nilkhet, and Azimpur.

The tribunal has issued arrest warrants for all eight accused. While three—retired judge AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik, Professor AKM Jamal Uddin, and Tanbir Hasan Shaikat—are already in custody, the others remain absconding.

Prosecution alleges that Maksud Kamal facilitated the involvement of Chhatra League activists in attacks on students after communicating with then-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

Dr Zafar Iqbal is accused of referring to protesting students as 'Razakars' and remaining silent during the killings, with prosecutors claiming evidence of his involvement in a conspiracy.

Justice Manik is accused of justifying police shootings by calling a victim, Abu Sayed, a 'terrorist' on a talk show, which the prosecution says legitimised further suppression.

Professor Jamal Uddin allegedly called for students to be 'drowned' in the Bay of Bengal and 'eliminated'.

The other accused, including BCL leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, are alleged to have directly participated in attacks on protesters.
